newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bond markets expectant before FOMC, expiry.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bond markets expectant before FOMC, expiry.

text.p: Implied volatility in bond options slipped on Friday ahead of a long weekend in France and Germany, but next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting may drive volatility higher, LIFFE traders said.
"You should sell volatility today or on Monday, but that's for the short-term. The FOMC meeting on Tuesday has the potential to upset the market," said one floor broker from a U.S. bank.
"With the BTP, Bund and gilt options expiring next week, it's a very interesting equation," he added.
June BTP options expire on Wednesday and June Bund and gilt options exercisable into June futures on Thursday.
The market is speculating on a U.S. rate rise at next Tuesday's FOMC meeting.
"I think the Fed will firm, but I don't know whether the market thinks that," the U.S. broker said.

Bund options volatility was a touch softer on Friday. Implied volatility of the September option exercisable into the September future was at 2.24 percent offered by 1100 GMT, said GNI, compared with an earlier 2.24 percent bid.
Implied volatility of June Bund options was quoted at 4.80 percent, and July and August serial months at 5.25 percent.
Volume was thin in advance of Monday's holiday in France, Germany and other parts of Northern Europe, floor traders said.
There were also few indicators on Friday, though the University of Michigan preliminary survey for May, to be released at 1400 GMT, had the capacity to move the market, they added.
"You can get a Friday squeeze, so it might be a bit perky this afternoon," said one broker from a European bank.
Futures markets were largely unmoved by a higher-than-forecast rise in April U.S. housing starts to 1.473 million.
Traders also shrugged off Germany's plans to revalue its gold reserves to bolster its finances ahead of European economic and monetary union (EMU).
